description: Ground-truth bug corpus for the skill-codex cross-model review eval. Each case seeds exactly ONE subtle, plausible bug a bias-to-ship model tends to wave through. expectedSignals drives the keyword matcher in src/matcher.ts: a review 'catches' a bug only when it names the bug location AND at least minSignalHits of the listed signal phrases.

cases.title: 1-based page treated as 0-based offset
cases.bug: start is computed as `page * size` instead of `(page - 1) * size`. Because the public API documents `page` as 1-based, page 1 skips the first `size` items and the final page is unreachable.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: The offset math is off by one page: with 1-based paging, start must be (page - 1) * size, otherwise page 1 silently drops the first window of items.

cases.title: Optional address dereferenced without a guard
cases.bug: address is declared optional (`address?`) but `.city` is read unconditionally, so any user without an address throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined'.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: user.address is optional and may be undefined; reading user.address.city without a guard throws at runtime for users with no address.

cases.title: Token refresh has no in-flight dedupe (thundering herd)
cases.bug: A `refreshing` promise field was added but never used. Concurrent getToken() callers all see token===null and each await their own refresh(), firing N redundant token fetches instead of sharing one.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: Concurrent callers each trigger their own refresh because the in-flight promise (refreshing) is never assigned or awaited; requests should share a single in-flight refresh to avoid a thundering herd / race.

cases.title: File handle leaks when a write rejects
cases.bug: The try/finally that guaranteed handle.close() was removed. If any handle.write() rejects, the function returns before close(), leaking the file descriptor.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: Without try/finally, a rejected write() skips handle.close(), leaking the file descriptor; close must run even on error.

cases.title: User input interpolated into SQL string
cases.bug: The parameterized query was replaced with string interpolation of `term`, which comes from the HTTP query string. This is a classic SQL injection.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: term is interpolated directly into the SQL string instead of being passed as a bound parameter, allowing SQL injection; use a parameterized/bound query.

cases.title: Catch-all swallows errors and returns null
cases.bug: A blanket try/catch was added that converts every failure (network error, HTTP 500, malformed JSON) into a `null` return, making real failures indistinguishable from an empty result.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: The bare catch swallows all errors and returns null, so callers cannot distinguish a failed request from an empty body; errors should propagate or be typed.

cases.title: Authorization check negated
cases.bug: The return is `!(isOwner || isAdmin)`. The permission is inverted: only users who are neither owner nor admin are allowed to delete, while the real owner and admins are denied.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: The boolean is inverted (leading !): canDelete returns true for users who are neither owner nor admin, granting deletes to strangers and denying the owner.

cases.title: Empty-list guard dropped, division by zero
cases.bug: The `if not values: return 0.0` guard was removed, so average([]) raises ZeroDivisionError instead of returning 0.0.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: The empty-list guard was removed; average([]) now divides by len([])==0 and raises ZeroDivisionError.

cases.title: Checksum accumulator narrowed to uint8
cases.bug: The accumulator type was changed from uint64 to uint8, which wraps modulo 256. For any input longer than a couple hundred bytes the checksum becomes effectively random and collides constantly.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: acc is uint8 and overflows (wraps mod 256) after the first ~256 bytes, so the checksum is wrong for any non-trivial input; accumulate in a wider type.

cases.title: Money summed in floating-point dollars
cases.bug: Integer-cent arithmetic was replaced with floating-point dollars (cents / 100) and rounded back at the end, introducing IEEE-754 rounding error that can shift a total by a cent.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: Converting cents to floating-point dollars and back introduces rounding error; money should stay in integer cents to avoid off-by-a-cent totals.

cases.title: Sanitization removed, path traversal in download
cases.bug: The filename sanitization (`replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9._-]/g, '')`) was removed and the user-controlled name is joined directly, so '../../etc/passwd' escapes the uploads directory.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: name is user-controlled and joined without sanitization or a containment check, so '../' sequences escape UPLOADS (path traversal); validate the resolved path stays within the base directory.

cases.title: Duplicate-email guard both un-awaited and inverted
cases.bug: The guard became `if (!isEmailTaken(email))`. isEmailTaken returns a Promise (no await), which is always truthy, so `!promise` is always false and the guard never throws — duplicate accounts are created. The misleading code comment rationalizes it as correct.
cases.correctReviewShouldFlag: isEmailTaken is not awaited (returns a truthy Promise) and the condition is negated, so the duplicate-email check never fires and duplicate accounts are created; await the call and use the un-negated condition.
